card.name: Animal study dose-level wording
card.fires_on: The word "at" or "doses" right after an animal species or study mention, just before an upper dose limit such as "up to". Found in animal toxicology and reproduction sections of drug labels.

modes.label: "at" after species
modes.description: The word "at" after rats, mice or rabbits, leading into a dose amount.
modes.example: Studies in rats<< at>> doses up to 54 μg

modes.label: "doses" after at or the
modes.description: The word "doses" introducing the tested dose range in a study.
modes.example: no adverse effects on embryo/fetal development were observed at<< doses>> of up to 16 mg/kg

card.writes: It promotes comparison and threshold words like "≥" and "negative", suggesting a dose limit or a no-effect result follows.
card.plain: It marks the spot in animal study sentences where the label is about to state the dose level tested.
